tagline: Push-to-talk dictation that lives in your tray.
description: Clean-room rebuild of a BYOK push-to-talk dictation app for Windows and macOS. Widget-first: the tray pill is the app, the window is for settings. Groq Whisper by default, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint supported. Merges the dictation core with the VFlow feature set (transcription log, usage analytics with live cost, WPM, recap notifications, wrap-up) reimplemented fresh. Copyright Eze Media LLC, GPLv3 from commit one, built entirely on LaBroi's personal machine. No code, prose, specs, or assets may be copied from ~/Projects/undertone, ~/Projects/the-peoples-voice-flow, or ~/Projects/OpenWhisp.

conventions.verify: npm run typecheck, npm run test, and npm run smoke must be green before any commit. Smoke prints SMOKE_RESULT JSON and every subsystem adds a named check.
conventions.stories: Work stories in order. Never set passes true until every acceptance criterion is verified; record how in notes. Stories with needs_human true get built and smoke-verified, then their human step is appended to HANDOFF.md and work continues.
conventions.commits: One commit per story minimum, prefixed with the story id. git pull --rebase before every commit. After changing prd.json run npm run roadmap.
conventions.cleanRoom: Never open or copy from the undertone, the-peoples-voice-flow, or OpenWhisp repos. Concepts yes, artifacts no. If blocked without them, stop and ask LaBroi.
conventions.style: No em dashes or spaced hyphens as clause separators anywhere. Night studio design tokens only, amber reserved for live states. The product name is always lowercase murmur in every user-visible surface, even at sentence start.

Remaining live: LaBroi confirms a tray Open murmur click raises the window above other apps in the installed build (HANDOFF.md). stories.title: Recording pipeline with warm mic
stories.description: A hidden audio renderer captures the mic to 16kHz mono WAV. The stream is pre-armed (warm mic) with a short ring buffer so the first syllable is never clipped. Handles sleep, resume, and device changes by re-arming automatically. Cancel discards audio. Smoke drives the pipeline with a synthetic source.
acceptance: Smoke check recording produces a valid WAV header and nonzero samples from a synthetic source
WAV encoder is unit tested (header fields, sample counts, mono 16k)
Resume and device-change events re-arm the stream without an app restart
Live: LaBroi confirms the first word of a fast press-and-speak is captured
stories.notes: automated criteria verified 2026-09-05: 8 WAV unit tests (encoder header fields, byte lengths, clamping, downsample 48k to 16k, parse rejects garbage). Smoke recording check green 3 consecutive runs: hidden capture window with synthetic oscillator produces valid 16k mono PCM16 WAV with pre-roll included, nonzero peak. Smoke recordingRearm green: main-driven rearm round trip re-arms the graph. powerMonitor resume triggers rearm; a dead track re-arms itself. Found and fixed: sandboxed preloads cannot load shared rollup chunks, channel literals now live inline per preload. Remaining live: first-syllable capture with a real mic (HANDOFF.md). LaBroi live-verified 2026-09-07: fast press-and-speak captures the first word. LaBroi reported 2026-09-09: after sleep and wake (both Mac and PC) the hotkey no longer captures audio. Root cause: the resume re-arm was single-shot with every failure path unhandled; getUserMedia right after wake commonly rejects or hangs while the OS audio stack re-enumerates, one failed attempt left the mic dead until restart, and a silently stalled graph (Windows modern standby) or a killed capture renderer had no detection at all. Fix 2026-09-09 (v0.1.5): chunk-liveness watchdog in the recorder (a healthy graph delivers chunks continuously; a stall re-arms with retry until chunks flow, hung attempts abandoned via a generation counter), all arm paths guarded, and main reloads the capture renderer on render-process-gone with escalating backoff. Review gate confirmed seven findings, all fixed: teardown now clears shared state synchronously before any await (a slow close could null a successor's live graph and orphan its stream), a recording in progress survives graph death as rate-tagged segments so a mid-take outage never loses captured speech, getUserMedia is acquired before the AudioContext so abandoned hung attempts cannot exhaust the per-page context cap, ready is decoupled from first-arm success, the revive backoff escalates by crash spacing instead of resetting on every ready, the recovery smoke check requires an outage ack so it cannot pass on an unbroken graph, and the docs no longer claim platform verification that has not happened. Verified after fixes: 8 liveness unit tests; smoke checks recordingRecovery (graph killed silently plus two forced arm failures, recovers unaided) and recordingRevive (renderer crashed, revives and records) green 3 consecutive runs. LaBroi live-verified 2026-09-12: after real sleep and wake on both the Mac and the PC, the hotkey captures audio normally again. Story fully complete.

stories.title: Insertion at the cursor
stories.description: Final text lands at the cursor in the focused app: save clipboard, set text, send the platform paste keystroke, restore the clipboard. macOS uses osascript keystroke (no compiled helper), Windows uses a no-compile keystroke path. A copy-only fallback setting exists. Insertion must never steal or shift focus.
acceptance: Clipboard save and restore logic is unit tested, including non-text clipboard content left untouched on failure
Smoke check insertion initializes the platform strategy
Copy-only mode puts the text on the clipboard and skips the keystroke
Live: LaBroi verifies insertion in three real apps per platform without focus loss
stories.notes: automated criteria verified 2026-09-05: 7 unit tests on the pure restore plan (clean restore, empty original, non-text payload untouched, user copy mid-insertion wins) and the platform keystroke builders (osascript cmd+v, powershell SendKeys, null elsewhere). Smoke insertion check runs the copy path end to end and restores the user clipboard; keystrokes are never fired in smoke by design. Paste failure fails open to copied, so text is never lost. Copy-only mode is a setting (insertion.mode). Remaining live: paste into three real apps per platform without focus loss (HANDOFF.md). LaBroi live-verified 2026-09-07: insertion confirmed in real apps, focus intact, clipboard restored. Fix 2026-09-07 (LaBroi field report: clipboard overwritten by dictations): the restore is now full fidelity. The old design skipped restoring whenever the clipboard held any non-text flavor, which on macOS is nearly every real copy (screenshots outright, and even plain text carries extra flavors), so restores rarely fired. The clipboard is now captured wholesale (all items, all MIME flavors, materialized before we overwrite, 32MB cap) and written back atomically after the paste settles; text is the fallback, a mid-insertion user copy still wins, and a screenshot copied before dictating now survives. Verified: rewritten planRestore unit tests plus the insertion smoke check now does a live capture-and-restore round trip. LaBroi reported 2026-09-12: a dictation transcribed and recorded to history but never appeared in the target app. Root cause: the paste keystroke posts the Cmd+V event and resolves, but the target app reads the pasteboard only when it processes that event, and there is no OS signal for the read (reading does not bump the change count). The 250ms inline settle lost that race on a loaded system (a macOS update was installing), so the clipboard restore landed before the app's paste read and the paste delivered stale content. Fix 2026-09-13: settle raised to 1500ms and moved to a background task so the inserted feedback stays immediate; insertText awaits any pending restore before capturing, so back-to-back dictations cannot interleave a restore with a fresh capture; planRestore's mid-dictation copy protection is unchanged. Verified: typecheck, 278 unit tests, smoke green 3 consecutive runs (insertion and dictationLoop checks included). Remaining live: LaBroi confirms a real dictation pastes into a busy app and the prior clipboard comes back about 1.5s later (HANDOFF.md). Review gate 2026-09-13 confirmed two findings, both fixed: the backgrounded restore swallowed errors silently (now logged loud via console.error, and the settle's clipboard read guarded like capture's), and a fast follow-on dictation could stall up to 1.5s awaiting the pending settle (insertText now flushes a sleeping settle before awaiting, so the wait is milliseconds; the predecessor's paste has had a full record-and-transcribe round to land by then). Re-verified after fixes: typecheck, 278 unit tests, smoke green. LaBroi live-verified 2026-09-17 in the installed walkthrough build: dictation pastes into a busy app with the prior clipboard returning after the settle, and back-to-back dictations both land. Story complete.

stories.title: Silence never inserts text
stories.description: An energy gate (RMS threshold plus minimum voiced duration) short-circuits before upload, and a transcript sanity filter (empty, whitespace, known Whisper hallucination phrases) short-circuits after. Either path shows a quiet no-speech state and inserts nothing.

Update 2026-09-06 (LaBroi field report of trailing injections): a two-layer tail defense shipped: deterministic stripping of trailing artifactTails sentences (a strict never-genuinely-spoken subset; the reviewer blocked a first version that would have eaten real thank-you sign-offs, and history now records the transcript exactly as heard), plus the polish validator rejecting outputs that end on a hallucination phrase the input did not end on. LaBroi live-verified 2026-09-06: the silence hold is good, nothing inserts. Update 2026-09-07 night: LaBroi caught a live injection; history showed a fabricated trailing Okay in the RAW transcript, so ASR-born. Genuinely dictatable words stay off the deterministic strip lists per the iron law; instead the cleanup model now carries a disconnected-trailing-filler rule (judgment layer, fails open) plus a never-introduce-em-dashes rule after it inserted one into his text. Validator test confirms a dropped trailing filler passes.

stories.title: Usage analytics and live cost card
stories.description: Aggregations over the event log power an analytics page: minutes dictated, words, sessions, and daily activity chart, plus a monthly usage card with a live cost estimate computed from shared/rates.json. Rates are verified against the provider pricing page and the check date is recorded in the file.
acceptance: Aggregation unit tests cover month boundaries, empty logs, and multi-day ranges

stories.notes: Verified 2026-09-05: 9 aggregation unit tests (month and today boundaries local-time and DST safe, zero-filled chronological 14-day series, empty log, cost math incl. the Groq 10-second ASR billing minimum, fallback rates, no compounding rounding). Analytics tab renders monthly card with live cost estimate, 14-day chart (cream emphasis, amber stays reserved), lifetime totals; summary computed in main so transcripts never reach the renderer for charts; smoke analytics check green. Review gate CRITICAL catch: the llama cleanup defaults had been decommissioned by Groq on 2026-08-16, confirmed against console.groq.com/docs/deprecations, meaning the cleanup pass had been silently failing open for all users; rates.json, defaults, UI suggestions, and docs repointed to openai/gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b (rates from the primary models page), plus an automatic settings migration for existing profiles. Also fixed per review: per-day minutes rounding no longer compounds (regression test added). Lesson recorded: verify against primary sources, secondary roundups quoted stale tables. Update 2026-09-06: lifetime avg wpm stat added and an 18-week GitHub-style activity heatmap (the mat) added to analytics at LaBroi's request, cream intensity ladder with today outlined, summary span widened to 126 days. Update 2026-09-06 round two: the wall gained GitHub parity at LaBroi's request: month and weekday labels, per-day hover with date and words, a period word total, and a year picker back to the first session (new analytics:heatmap channel with a pure heatmap() range function, smoke-checked). One test expectation corrected during build: a Cleaned text colon intro rejects as meta chatter (the earlier guard), so the preamble-rule case uses a neutral colon intro. Remaining live criterion: LaBroi dictates both list shapes into a plain text field and a markdown app (HANDOFF.md). Review gate 2026-09-13 confirmed one finding, fixed: the no-period-on-list-endings rule in ensureTerminal ran unconditionally, so a raw transcript already starting a line with a dash would have changed output with the toggle off; the rule is now gated on smartLists and two parity vectors lock both directions. Re-verified after the fix: typecheck clean, 290 unit tests, smoke green. Live incident 2026-09-14: LaBroi's first real smart-list dictations came back as prose. Root cause found by replaying his exact transcripts against the same model (gpt-oss-120b, Groq serving, same system prompt and temperature): the model frequently DROPPED the spoken intro sentence (I want to make a checklist) while forming the list, and losing those words pushed the output under the validator's 0.6 length-ratio floor, so the transformation was correctly rejected and fell back to prose. Fix: SMART_LISTS_PROMPT gains an explicit layout-only rule (forming a list never drops spoken words; the intro stays as the intro line). Replay after the fix: 12 of 12 trials produced correct list shapes and 11 of 12 pass validation (the twelfth over-compresses items and falls back to prose, the safe direction). The ratio floor stays untouched: it is the deletion and injection defense, and it did its job here. Verified after fix: typecheck clean, 303 tests, smoke green. Refinement 2026-09-14 after LaBroi's live feedback (items carried scaffolding like then bacon, and some lists collapsed to comma runs): the prompt now tells the model entries keep only the words that name them, enumeration words and lead-ins dissolve into the list shape (the one sanctioned exception to keeping every word, entries themselves never dropped or reworded), anchored by a literal example; validatePolish gives a deeper 0.4 ratio floor ONLY to list-shaped output under smart lists (at least two list lines, at most one intro prose line), since scaffolding legitimately disappears there, while prose keeps the strict 0.6 floor. Replay on the live model: 6 of 6 sequence trials return exactly the clean requested shape (intro colon line, bare items), 2 of 3 packing trials bullet with the third staying prose (the safe direction), prose controls never get forced into lists. Three new unit tests pin the deeper floor's accept and both reject directions. Review gate on the refinement confirmed a real content-loss window, closed: the deeper floor is now earned only when the input itself enumerated (two or more implied entries, the stronger of enumerator words and comma runs) AND the output carries at least that many list lines; a list missing an implied entry rejects as missing entries, and prose the speaker never enumerated keeps the strict floor even when restyled as a fake list. Two new adversarial unit tests pin both closures (308 total green). Live-found 2026-09-15 (LaBroi's grocery dictation): the implied-entry comma heuristic counted the intro comma (For my grocery list,) so a perfect four line answer from the model was rejected as missing entries three times out of three in replay. Fixed by dropping the plus one from the comma count (undercounting only weakens the floor, the safe direction); a regression test pins the grocery shape. The polish pass also gained fallback observability: every fall-back now reports its reason (http status, validate: reason, timeout, network) through an onFallback callback that maybePolish writes to logs/murmur.log, so model-versus-validator questions read straight from the log instead of replay archaeology. Gate on the comma fix proved the first cut over-corrected (a plain Oxford run has N minus 1 commas for N items, so dropping the plus one let a dropped entry pass, violating the iron law). Final rule: item commas keep the plus one, but a comma that starts a clause (followed by I, we, you, let's, please) is excluded from the count; the bias when heuristics miss is overcounting, because an over-rejected list falls back to prose and loses nothing. Both regression tests pinned: the grocery intro-comma acceptance and the Oxford dropped-entry rejection (312 tests green). stories.title: A silent stream heals itself
stories.description: Root-caused live 2026-09-15 with the US-047 diagnostics: murmur's warm mic stream, armed at launch, kept delivering digital silence (peak 0.0002 across five dictations) after Wave Link reconfigured the device underneath it, with no device-change event to trigger the existing re-arm, so only an app relaunch revived capture. The chunk-liveness watchdog cannot see this: chunks flow, they are just dead. The heal: when a dictation ends in nospeech with a dead-zero peak (below 0.001, an order of magnitude under any real room's noise floor), main requests a capture re-arm on the spot through the same channel the US-008 machinery already serves, so the NEXT press gets a live stream without a relaunch. The delivered breadcrumb also gains the peak, so faint-but-passing audio (the Whisper hallucination zone) stops masquerading as healthy.

stories.title: Keys live with their providers
stories.description: Directed by LaBroi 2026-09-16 after the single key slot kept confusing every provider switch: saving a key for one provider silently replaced another's. Keys become a ring: each saved key is stored encrypted under the base URL it belongs to, the setup tab's key field always speaks for the ACTIVE provider (no key yet, or its own masked key), and beneath it every saved key appears as a line item labeled with its provider name and mask, each with its own remove. Switching providers brings that provider's key along automatically, for both the speech connection and the separate cleanup connection (one ring keyed by base URL serves both). Migration: the legacy single key assigns itself by its own full prefix when unambiguous (gsk_ is Groq), else by recorded provenance, else it surfaces as an unassigned key the user can assign to the current provider or remove; nothing is ever silently dropped. This retires the provenance and mask-inference workarounds structurally: a ring cannot lose track of whose key is whose. The keyring is free (BYOK setup stays fully free); Pro profiles keep their value as named whole setups.

stories.title: Brain dump: speak a note instead of a paste
stories.description: Shaped with LaBroi 2026-09-17, design settled 2026-09-18. A second global chord (captured in settings under the paste-last chord's rules: a regular key plus modifiers, never containing the dictation hotkey, distinct from the other chords) starts a note dictation: same mic, same hold or toggle trigger, same pipeline, and the same formatting a dictation gets (dictionary, deterministic formatting, cleanup, expansions, all failing open to the raw transcript; LaBroi decision: one pipeline produces one kind of text everywhere). Only the destination differs: instead of pasting, the text appends to a markdown file in the user's notes folder. Obsidian integration is the folder itself: a vault is a plain folder of markdown files and Obsidian shows whatever appears in it, running or not, so any folder works (Obsidian, Logseq, iCloud Drive). Settings gets a notes section: the note chord, a notes folder row (native folder picker, the path in an editable field, Clear; empty keeps note mode dormant), a status line naming where the last note landed, Open today's inbox, and an Advanced layout with a path template relative to the folder (default murmur/inbox/{date}.md), an entry template (default a ## {time} heading over the text), the tokens {date} {time} {datetime} {year} {month} {day} {text}, a live preview of today's resolved path, and Reset to default. Guardrails: a resolved path stays inside the folder, ends in .md or .txt, and a template that fails to resolve falls back to the default with a log line; path tokens render filename-safe ({time} becomes 10-32 inside a path). Writes are append-only so synced vaults never see a whole-file rewrite, missing subfolders are created, and the filename date is local time. The overlay shows a distinct note state (gold pill edge, a note tag beside the timer, noted on success) with its own start and save cues; a note chord pressed with no folder set shows an overlay hint and plays the soft no-speech cue instead of silently doing nothing. Iron law inherited from the formatter: the words land on disk before anything else happens; if the folder is unreachable the note lands in murmur's own data folder under notes/ and the diagnostics log names the redirect, and the status line says so. Note dictations join history tagged as notes (so paste-last works and the words count toward belts) and a tray item opens today's inbox. No external accounts, no sync, no routing in this story; an {app} token and an obsidian:// deep link are follow-on candidates.

stories.notes: Built 2026-09-18 on feature/brain-dump (LaBroi directive: feature work on its own branch, merged once live-verified). shared/notes.ts holds the pure template math (noteMoment, renderTemplate, resolveNotePath with the path guard, renderNoteEntry with the never-lost default, appendSeparator) and the NOTE_FOLDER_HINT constant; settings.notes carries binding, folder, pathTemplate, entryTemplate; the note chord is a second HotkeyDispatcher plus trigger machine under the shared chordRefusal rules (needs a key, cannot contain a modifier-only dictation binding, cannot equal the dictation binding or the paste chord); dictation.ts carries a session kind so the other chord's stop is a no-op, and a note delivers through saveNote (folder, then userData/notes, then history keeps the words regardless); the overlay machine gained a mode (dictation or note) and a hint phase from rest; cues noteStart and noted; history events carry kind note; the tray shows Open today's inbox while a folder is set; settings has the notes panel (chord, picker plus editable path, last-note status, Open today's inbox, file layout with a live preview and Reset to default) and the home tab marks notes; docs/notes.md is question-first and linked from README and settings.md. Two live-found fixes followed the same day, unit and smoke verified (367 tests, smoke green): the hold trigger now latches from key down to key up whatever start said, because OS key repeat had retried the refused dormant start every 85ms (seventeen hints and cues in two seconds); and the notes folder itself must already exist before a write, because mkdir had been creating missing parents and would have recreated a renamed vault or an unplugged drive as a ghost folder instead of redirecting (notesFallback now covers a missing folder: fallback, ENOENT logged, no ghost). stories.title: Brain dump sorting: thoughts file themselves
stories.description: Shaped with LaBroi 2026-09-17, design settled 2026-09-20. A notes setting, Sort into tasks and ideas (default off), turns the sorter on: after a note lands (US-050) and the pill has said noted, a background pass sends the note's sentences to a model as a numbered list and the model only classifies, it never writes: it replies with JSON assigning each number one of task, idea, or note. murmur then copies the original sentences, untouched, into the right files: tasks as checkbox lines to murmur/todo.md, ideas as dash lines to murmur/ideas.md, each with a markdown link back to the inbox note (relative to the file, link text the note's time). The inbox stays verbatim forever (LaBroi decision, option A): it is the log, todo.md is the working list, so tasks appear in both and nothing is ever rewritten in a synced vault. The validator is strict and pure: every sentence assigned exactly once, only the three labels, anything else (chatter, a code fence around nothing, a missing or invented number, a bad label) rejects the whole sort, touches no file, and logs a reason; a failed connection does the same. Sorting runs on whichever base the note landed in (the vault, or the data folder after a redirect). The sort connection mirrors the cleanup slot: Same as cleanup by default (which already resolves to the cleanup slot or the speech provider), or a separate base URL and model with its key served by the ring under that base URL. The tasks and ideas paths join the File layout section as templates under the inbox path's guard. Settings shows the outcome on the Last note line (filed 2 tasks 1 idea, or sort rejected with the reason) and a Sort again button re-runs the sort on the newest note. Off is a first-class mode for people who keep raw notes and feed them to their own tools. Explicitly out: Notion, Apple Notes, MCP routing, conversational recall, rewording of any kind.
acceptance: Pure sort logic in shared/sorter.ts is unit tested: sentence splitting (newlines, terminators, list lines kept whole), the numbered prompt, validateSort accepting a complete labeling and rejecting chatter, bad JSON, missing numbers, extra numbers, and bad labels, relative links from the tasks file to the inbox file, and the filed line shapes

With sorting on, a note sorts into checkbox tasks and dash ideas across the two files with links back, wording unchanged, and the inbox entry is never modified (smoke-checked against a mock model: noteSort)
A rejected or failed sort touches no file and logs a reason with the model name; sorting off writes nothing beyond the inbox (smoke-checked)

The sort connection defaults to the cleanup connection and accepts its own base URL and model with the key served by the ring; the settings rows for it reuse the cleanup connection rows (smoke-checked resolution: separate slot when complete, cleanup otherwise)
Settings: the Sort toggle (default off), the connection rows, tasks and ideas paths in File layout with Reset to default, the sort outcome on the Last note line, and Sort again

Topic headings (LaBroi 2026-09-20): with Name each note on, the sort model's short name for a note lands in the heading's {topic} slot in BOTH files and nowhere else; a name that is empty, long, many-worded, or carrying markdown is dropped and the note still files under the rest of the heading (unit tests cover the sanitizer and the reserved key, smoke covers a good name and a refused one)
Docs updated: how sorting works and why nothing is reworded, the two files and their link format, turning it off for raw-notes workflows, the connection, and what a rejected sort means
Live: LaBroi dumps a mixed ramble (todos plus ideas plus a stray thought) and finds each piece in the right file with its source link, then turns sorting off and confirms a note writes the inbox only
stories.notes: Built 2026-09-20 on feature/brain-dump. shared/sorter.ts is the pure half: splitSentences (one unit per line, prose split at terminators, list lines kept whole, titles and Latin shorthands like Dr. and e.g. never split), numberedList, SORT_SYSTEM_PROMPT (label only, never rewrite, dictated instructions are content), validateSort (every number exactly once, only the three labels, JSON extracted from a fenced or chatty reply), relativeLink (per-segment percent encoding so spaces and hashes survive), taskLine and ideaLine (existing list markers stripped so lines never double up), planFiling. main/notes/sorter.ts resolves the connection (separate slot when enabled, complete, and holding a ring key, else whatever the cleanup pass would use, else none), asks the model, validates, and copies; main/notes/files.ts holds the append-only writer shared with the inbox. settings.notes gains sort (default off), tasksTemplate, ideasTemplate, and a connection block; the cleanup connection rows were extracted to renderer/settings/ConnectionRows.tsx and now render both slots, with generic ring IPC (apikey:setFor, statusFor, clearFor, provider:testFor) so a third slot can hold its own key without touching the speech or cleanup slots' keys. The sort runs in the background after the pill says noted, on whichever base the note landed in; the inbox is never rewritten (LaBroi decision, option A). Verified: typecheck clean; 385 unit tests (18 sorter cases incl. adversarial replies, abbreviations, link encoding); smoke green on three consecutive runs, 49 checks, the new ones being noteSort (off writes nothing; a valid labeling files two tasks and one idea with links and leaves the inbox byte-identical; a filed note refuses a re-file; an unopenable ideas file fails with zero tasks landed; two overlapping sorts join one run; chatter and http 500 each touch no file) and sortConnection (separate wins only when complete with a key, else cleanup, else null). Screenshots through MURMUR_SETTINGS_ANCHOR show the sort rows and confirm the extracted cleanup rows render unchanged. Review gate 2026-09-20: one CONFIRMED (a failed ideas write could leave tasks behind while the UI said nothing filed; both files are now opened for append before either is written, so only a disk filling mid-write can land a partial, and then the status says exactly what landed) and four judgment calls applied (one sort at a time with a shared in-flight promise, and Sort again withdrawn once a note is filed, so no double filing; a cleanup base URL left behind with cleanup on Same no longer blocks saving a sort key; abbreviations no longer split; a non-JSON 200 reports its own reason). Nits applied: hashes encoded in links, the four generic channels listed in shared/ipc.ts, docs quote the real log line prefixes, a tasks or ideas path equal to the inbox path warns in the preview. Deliberately kept: lenient JSON extraction from a chatty reply (labels only, nothing reworded; documented). Amended 2026-09-20 after LaBroi reviewed the file shape before his live check: filed lines group under a heading, default '## {date}' in settings.notes.filedHeadingTemplate, written once per file per day so a day's dumps gather together and a long list stays navigable; clearing the field gives one flat list. Pure helpers renderFiledHeading and headingPrefix are unit tested (a heading already carried anywhere in the file is never repeated, a longer line that starts with it does not count), the noteSort smoke check proves a second same-day dump joins the existing heading, and the layout rows now read Inbox file, Tasks file, Ideas file, Group under, then Entry. Default file layout stays todo.md and ideas.md beside the inbox folder (LaBroi 2026-09-20: a to-do list works as one list; a folder per stream is one path edit away). Topic headings added the same day at LaBroi's request (a date alone does not say what a group is about): settings.notes.topicHeadings, default off, asks the sort model for a name of at most five plain words under a reserved topic key in the same reply, sanitizeTopic strips markdown and control characters and refuses anything long or many-worded, and renderFiledHeading collapses the gap so {topic} with no topic leaves the date standing alone. The name reaches the heading only; sentences are still copied verbatim, and a refused name never fails a sort. Both the tasks and the ideas file carry the same heading, so one note's tasks and ideas sit under one name. The inbox keeps its time heading because the words are written before any model runs. stories.title: A silent stream heals before the first press
stories.description: Root-caused live 2026-09-17 at 10:03 PM from the US-047 log: after the Mac woke, the resume re-arm rebuilt the capture graph and chunks flowed, but the stream carried digital silence. The first press measured peak 0.0129 (nospeech, above the 0.001 dead-stream floor, so the US-048 heal did not fire) and the second measured 0.0002 (the heal fired). Two presses lost before capture came back. The chunk-liveness watchdog (US-008) is blind to this by design: chunks flow, they are just empty. The US-048 heal only runs after a press. Widening its floor is not the answer: the measured quiet-room floor is 0.004 and the speech gate's own RMS threshold is 0.01, so any floor high enough to catch 0.0129 would re-arm on real silence in real rooms. The fix is a second watchdog beside the first: every freshly installed graph must carry sustained signal (a run of chunks at or above the US-048 floor; a quiet room's noise floor qualifies in well under a tenth of a second, a single wake pop like the incident's 0.0129 does not) within a short window measured in the stream's own clock, or it is rebuilt, bounded by a retry budget so a hardware-muted mic or a truly silent room cannot loop forever. It rides every arm (launch, resume, track ended, the press-time heal). A graph that has proven itself is trusted from then on: going quiet later is a pause or a noise gate (NVIDIA Broadcast, Krisp, and macOS Voice Isolation output digital zero between words, and rebuilding on every pause would churn them), so a stream that truly dies mid-session stays with the US-048 press-time heal, whose rebuilt stream is then held to the same rule. Main sends nothing new. Reshaped by the 2026-09-18 review gate from a first cut that measured silence in wall time (it would have claimed chunk stalls in the 3 to 5 second band) and judged every graph continuously (it would have rebuilt gated mic paths five times per pause).
acceptance: Pure decision logic in liveness.ts (signalAction) is unit tested in the stream's own clock: probing while a fresh graph is inside its window or has delivered no chunks, a chunk stall freezes the verdict (the chunk watchdog owns stalls), rearm once silent chunks have flowed past the window with budget left, a single pop is not proof, exhausted once the budget is spent and a rebuild cannot reopen it, live once sustained signal arrives even after exhaustion, a proven graph stays live when it goes quiet later, and the shipped defaults keep a tick inside the window, proof beyond a pop, and a budget of at least three

The recorder rebuilds a dead-flat stream unaided: a new smoke check (recordingSilentHeal) replaces the live graph with one that flows at the incident's 0.0002, proves the damage (a recording through it shows chunks present and a peak under the floor), then proves the recovery (a later recording peaks above 0.05) with no message from main after the seam. Existing recording, rearm, recovery, and revive checks stay green

Bounded and quiet: one log line when a silent outage starts, one when the budget is exhausted, no per-tick lines; a re-arm requested by main (resume or the press-time heal) opens a fresh budget and a fresh pair of lines, so a heal that did not help is visible

The chunk watchdog and the signal watchdog never fight: the signal probe judges only an installed graph, only while the chunk watchdog reads healthy, only between recordings, and in chunk time, so a stalled, arming, or torn-down graph is handled by one path at a time and a take in progress is never torn down underneath by the signal probe
Docs: the sleep answer, the managed-audio answer, and the recovery answer in troubleshooting describe the two watchdogs, what the silent log lines mean, and the hardware-mute case
Live: LaBroi sleeps and wakes the Mac, waits ten seconds, and the FIRST press delivers; the log shows at most one silent re-arm line from the wake and then a delivered line with a healthy peak
stories.notes: Built 2026-09-18 within the hour of the live root cause (US-047 log, wake at 22:03 local: nospeech peak 0.0129 with no heal, then nospeech 0.0002 with the heal). Verified: typecheck clean; 337 unit tests (12 signalAction cases including stall freezes the verdict, single pop is not proof, proven graph stays live, a rebuild cannot reopen the budget); smoke green 3 consecutive runs on the final tree with recordingSilentHeal proving damage (chunks present, peak under 0.001) then recovery (peak above 0.05) and recording, rearm, recovery, revive, dictationLoop intact; kept-profile evidence runs show exactly one audio capture is silent line, one stalled line (from recordingRecovery), zero exhaustion lines. Review gate 2026-09-18, first pass: one CONFIRMED (wall-time silence would have claimed chunk stalls in the 3 to 5 second band and could fire with no graph installed), two judgment calls (continuous judging would rebuild gated mic paths five times per pause; rearm reopened the budget without the log flags), three nits (HANDOFF wait, damage recording margin, zero as never). All applied: chunk time plus the ctx and active guards; judge only unproven graphs, with sustained-signal proof as a builder addition over the reviewer's option because the incident's own 0.0129 pop would otherwise have marked the wake graph real; flags reset on main-driven rearm; ten seconds in HANDOFF and the live criterion; 700ms damage recording; signalChunks starts at 0. Re-verification pass: all six CONFIRMED-FIXED; follow-ons applied: recovery wait 2500ms with a corrected timeline comment, forty seconds for the budget check, criterion 4 scoped to the signal probe, docs say gates can output zero. Gate awareness, accepted: a graph that dies mid-session after proof is heal-only, and the US-048 heal judges the take by peak, so a mid-session death whose first take carries a single pop still costs two presses (follow-up candidate in US-048 territory: judge the take by sustained signal the same way); exposure for gated or hardware-muted mics is at most five rebuilds per launch or main-driven arm, then quiet until sound; signal chunks count cumulatively, so a dead graph accumulating twenty stray pops over minutes reads live until the next dead take reopens the budget. stories.title: Speak an edit: transform the text you have selected
stories.description: Shaped with LaBroi 2026-09-20, to build AFTER the brain dump branch (US-050 to US-052) merges, on its own branch. A third chord turns a selection into the subject of a spoken instruction: select text in any app, hold the chord, say what you want done ("turn this into a formatted list with actionable steps", "tighten this paragraph", "reply to this politely and decline"), and the transformed text replaces the selection. murmur already owns every part but one: the chord rules, the mic and transcription, an LLM connection with a key per provider, and an insertion path that pastes at the cursor and restores the clipboard. The new part is reading the selection: a synthetic copy keystroke through the existing insertion plan, then the clipboard, then the user's clipboard restored exactly as paste already does. Two rules shape the design. First, the roles invert from dictation and they must stay separate in the request: the SPOKEN words are the instruction, the SELECTED text is data that is never obeyed, so a document containing "ignore the above" cannot drive the model. Second, the cleanup validator's never-lose-words rule cannot apply to a transform that rewrites on purpose, so it is replaced by recoverability: the original selection is recorded in history before the model is called and reachable with the paste-last chord, and an empty, chatty, or refused response leaves the selection untouched with a reason in the log. The transform connection follows the cleanup and sort slots (same as cleanup by default, optionally its own base URL, model, and ring key). Honest failure where a copy keystroke yields nothing (some terminals, locked-down windows): the clipboard did not change, so the overlay says the selection could not be read and nothing is sent. Open questions for the build: whether the overlay shows the instruction while speaking, whether a long selection is capped with a warning, and whether a transform history entry should be distinguishable from a dictation on the home tab.

stories.title: One sentence, several tasks: splitting that cannot reword
stories.description: Live-found 2026-09-20, the evening US-051 passed; redesigned 2026-09-21 so it works on every sort connection, including the decision model of US-057. A brain dump speaks in comma runs ("tomorrow we are getting groceries, getting tacos, and going to the playground"), and the sorter's unit is the sentence, so that files as one checkbox instead of three. Smart lists does not rescue it: the cleanup prompt is told never to force a list onto ordinary prose, and a run of activities inside one flowing sentence reads as prose, which the live inbox text confirms. A different sort model changes nothing, because murmur never asks anyone to split a sentence. The first draft of this story had the model hand back the pieces as verbatim text and murmur check each piece against the sentence. That is dropped, for two reasons: a decision model cannot return text at all, and a chat model that picks its own pieces can leave words out, which is rewording by omission. Instead the code does the cutting and the model only votes. For each sentence labeled a task or an idea, murmur finds the candidate seams itself: a comma or semicolon followed by a space, or the connectors and, then, also between two runs of words, with compound forms such as ", and then" counting as one seam. Each seam gets one yes/no question, whether it separates two distinct items the speaker would act on separately, and murmur cuts only at the seams that came back yes, removing the seam text itself and nothing else. Every word the speaker said lands on exactly one line, in order, so the never-reword law holds by construction rather than by validation, and each line carries its own source link like any filed line. On a chat connection murmur numbers the seams in the prompt and the votes ride the reply already being made, under a reserved key holding the numbers of the confirmed seams, at no extra call or latency; the reserved key holds numbers only and is never a place the model can put text. On a decision connection (US-057) each seam is one Noul in the same request as the labels, with the two sides of the seam passed as structured fields of the question. The vote shape both connections produce is the same, a list of confirmed seam numbers per sentence, so the cutter never knows which model voted. A sentence with no candidate seam, no confirmed seam, or a malformed vote files whole as one line, per sentence, never failing the sort. Settings: the splitting rides the sort toggle; no new switch unless the live run asks for one.

Cutting at confirmed seams is pure and unit tested: every word of the sentence lands on exactly one line in order with only the seam text removed, a sentence with no confirmed seam stays whole, and a vote naming a seam that does not exist is rejected for that sentence only

stories.title: Sorting on a decision model, optional
stories.description: Shaped with LaBroi 2026-09-21 after researching TypeSafe AI, whose Jev model came out of stealth 2026-09-15. The sorter asks a chat model for strict JSON and then spends most of its code defending against what a chat model can do wrong: markdown fences, chatter wrapped around the object, a fourth label, a reworded sentence. Jev is a decision model rather than an LLM: it takes the note as state, one Choice question per sentence over the fixed answer space task, idea, note, and returns typed values with calibrated probabilities in 70 to 500ms for roughly a hundredth of a cent per note. The answer space is declared in the request, so a label outside it is not something the model declines to emit, it is something it cannot emit. This story is the swap only, with behavior identical to US-051: all-or-nothing filing, the same three labels, and the chat sorter staying both the default and the fallback. Jev gives up string generation entirely, so one feature does not cross to this path: the {topic} heading from US-051, which needs the model to name the note. On a decision connection {topic} renders empty and the panel says so rather than letting it quietly stop working. US-056 splitting crosses cleanly, because that story was redesigned so the model only votes yes or no per seam and never returns text; on a decision connection those votes are one Noul per seam in the same request as the labels, with the two sides of the seam passed as structured fields of the question. TypeSafe joins shared/provider-catalog.json under a third kind alongside stt and llm, so the preset dropdown, the verified-on date, and the weekly rate-verification Action cover it like any other provider; its input-only pricing maps onto the existing inputPerMTok and outputPerMTok fields, so the cost preview works with no new estimator code. Early access is waitlisted, so this stays strictly optional and off by default: a fresh clone with no TypeSafe key behaves exactly as it does today.

stories.title: Low-confidence lines stay in the inbox
stories.description: Shaped with LaBroi 2026-09-21; this is the reason a second protocol is worth carrying at all. US-051 sorts all or nothing: validateSort rejects the entire reply unless every sentence is labeled, so a single ambiguous line sends a whole note back to the inbox and the user re-runs it hoping for a better roll. A chat model cannot fix this, because it has no honest confidence to report and will assert a label either way. A decision model returns a probability distribution over the answer space on every Choice, and a flat distribution is exactly what an ambiguous line looks like from the inside. This story spends that signal: on a decision connection only, lines at or above a threshold file and lines below stay in the inbox, so a note sorts partially instead of not at all. The risk lives in Sort again. lastFiledInput is a whole-note guard today, so a second run after a partial file would append the already-landed lines a second time; it becomes a per-line guard before anything else here is built. The inbox itself stays verbatim as US-051 requires, so a held line is never marked up on disk: the count and the reason live in the report and the panel.
acceptance: A confidence threshold setting on the sort connection, shown only for a decision connection, with a stated default and copy explaining what falling below it means
Lines at or above the threshold file normally; lines below are left in the inbox untouched, and both the sort report and the settings panel say how many were held
A note whose every line falls below the threshold behaves exactly as a rejected sort does today, with nothing written to any file
Sort again re-runs only the held lines and never re-files a landed one: the whole-note lastFiledInput guard becomes per-line, unit tested against a partial file followed by a second sort
The inbox file is not annotated for held lines: it stays the verbatim record US-051 promises, unit tested
Docs updated: what a held line is, why it was held, how to file it by hand or by re-sorting, and that the threshold applies only to a decision connection

stories.title: Duplicates and completions: suggestions, never silent edits
stories.description: Shaped with LaBroi 2026-09-20, written 2026-09-21, and sequenced after US-058 because it extends that story's held lines. A brain dump next week touches items already in todo.md: the same errand said again, or a sentence that reports an item done ("I called the dentist"). Today both file as fresh checkboxes, so the list grows duplicates and finished work sits unticked. murmur must not guess: the checkbox is the only truth about completion, and nothing in a vault file is edited without a click. So the sort compares before it files. The open items of the tasks file and the ideas file (the most recent sixty of each, numbered, ticked items included with their state) ride the same request as the labels, and for every sentence labeled a task or an idea the model votes one relation against that list: new, same as item N, or completes item N. The model chooses from numbers only; it returns no text here either. New lines file exactly as US-051 does. A line voted same or completes is held in the inbox, which is already verbatim, so holding costs nothing and marks nothing up on disk; the sort report and the settings panel say how many were held and why, with the matched item quoted from the file: "looks like a duplicate of: Call the dentist about Thursday", "sounds like you finished: Renew the domain", or, when the match is a ticked item, "you finished this before". Each held line offers exactly the actions that keep every write explicit: File it anyway (one line lands, with its link, through the per-line path US-058 built) and Skip; a completion adds Tick it, which is the first in-place edit murmur ever makes to a vault file: the matched line's [ ] becomes [x], nothing else in the file changes byte for byte, the write goes to a temp file and renames into place, a copy of the file as it was is kept in the data folder for one day, and the action is refused with a reason if the file changed on disk since it was read. No text is ever merged: two lines that say the same thing become one by skipping the second, never by rewriting either. On a chat connection the votes ride the existing reply under a reserved key of numbers; on a decision connection (US-057) each candidate line is one Choice over the answer space new, same, completes, with a second Choice for the item number when it is not new. The vote shape both connections produce is identical, so the holder never knows which model voted. A malformed vote for a line means new, so a bad reply can never hide a line; a vote naming an item number that does not exist is treated the same way. A tick suggestion that turns out wrong costs one click to undo in the editor, and a duplicate suggestion that turns out wrong costs one File it anyway, so the worst case of a bad vote is a moment of the user's attention, never lost or altered words. Reminders (US-052) read the file the same way and see a tick the moment it lands.
acceptance: The comparison context is pure and unit tested: open and ticked items of both files are numbered in file order, capped at the most recent sixty per file with the cap stated in the prompt, each carrying its state and stripped of its source link; an empty or missing file yields an empty context and every line votes new by construction

Vote validation is pure and unit tested: new, same N, and completes N are accepted with N inside the context; a malformed vote, an unknown relation, or an out-of-range N means new for that line only; a line labeled note is compared for completion only: a past-tense report can complete an item and is held with Tick it and Skip, but a note is never a duplicate, since it files nowhere

A line voted same or completes is held, not filed: the inbox stays byte-identical, the tasks and ideas files gain only the new lines, and the sort report counts held lines with their reasons and matched items (smoke-checked against a mock model on both a duplicate and a completion)

The settings panel lists each held line with the matched item quoted and offers File it anyway and Skip, plus Tick it for a completion; File it anyway lands exactly that one line with its link through the per-line path and never a second time (smoke-checked)

Tick it changes only the matched line's box from [ ] to [x], leaves every other byte of the file unchanged, writes through a temp file and rename, keeps a dated copy of the prior file in the data folder, and refuses with a reason when the file changed since it was read (unit tested on the pure diff, smoke-checked on the write)

A related line the same reply also cut is cut first and its pieces compared in a second request on the same connection, so only the matching piece is held and the rest file; if that request cannot be answered the whole line is held carrying its pieces and File it anyway lands one line per piece (unit tested on the pure steps, smoke-checked on the chat path, the failure path, and the decision path)

On a chat connection the votes ride the existing reply under a reserved key of numbers only; a reply without the key behaves exactly as US-058 leaves it (unit tested); on a decision connection the votes are Choices in the same request (unit tested at the shared vote boundary)

Docs updated: what a held line is here, the three suggestions and what each button does, that no text is ever merged, that the checkbox is the only truth about completion, and that Tick it is the one in-place edit murmur makes and how it is kept safe

The automated criteria verified; the live criterion is queued in HANDOFF.md. stories.title: A spoken list files as items under its lead-in
stories.description: Live-found 2026-09-23 while checking US-057. The same spoken list lands in todo.md two different ways, depending on how the cleanup model wrote it. When cleanup makes it a list ("I need to buy:" over dash lines), the heading was filed as its own checkbox (patched the same day by dropping the heading). When cleanup keeps a sentence ("I need to buy apples, rice, and coffee."), US-056 cuts at the seams and keeps every word, so the lead-in rides the first item ("I need to buy apples", "rice", "coffee."). Decided with LaBroi 2026-09-23: both shapes converge on one result, the lead-in written as a plain line (never a checkbox) with the items as checkboxes nested under it, so the context stays in todo.md and reminders count only the items. For a sentence the model cut into two or more pieces, the model points at the word where the first item begins (a number only, never text: a Choice over the first side's word numbers on a decision connection, a reserved numeric key on a chat connection), and the words before it become the lead-in. Every word still lands exactly once: the lead-in in the lead line, the items below it. The final period of a cut run is trimmed so the items match. A list heading from cleanup becomes the lead line of the list lines under it. A missing, malformed, or first-word answer means no lead-in, exactly the US-056 behavior. Pieces compared against filed items (US-055) are compared bare, and a held piece keeps its lead-in so File it anyway nests it too. A lead line is never read back as an item (duplicate compare, reminders, tick).
acceptance: Pure and unit tested: splitting a cut run into a lead-in and items keeps every word exactly once, trims only the run's final period, and a start at word 1, out of range, or on a sentence left whole yields no lead-in
A list heading from cleanup becomes the lead line for the list lines under it, never a unit sent to the model

Both connections can point at the first item: a decision request carries one Choice per sentence with seams over its first side's word numbers, a chat reply carries a reserved numeric key; malformed answers mean no lead-in for that sentence only, never a failed sort

Filing writes the lead-in once as a plain line ending in a colon, with that run's tasks nested as checkboxes under it in todo.md and its ideas nested as bullets in ideas.md; a line with no lead-in files flat as before
Reading files back ignores lead lines: duplicate compare, reminders, and tick count only real items, nested ones included
A held piece keeps its lead-in and File it anyway nests it under that lead-in
Docs: the notes page explains the lead-in and shows the nested shape
